notes.decision: Translated as 'ploughed-field.' This Lyc. lexeme parallels ⲕⲁⲍ 'land' in line 8 (third land = the Church) as the cosmic-zone-noun for the soul. Likely from ⲱϩⲉ 'plough/standing-field' (Crum 535b ⲟⲩⲱⲱϩⲉ). The kephalaion's pervasive agricultural register (farmers, fields, fruits, harvest) supports the agricultural reading over a more abstract 'dwelling.'

Translated as 'doing farmer's work / acting as farmer.' Hapax compound: ⲣ̄- ('do') + ⲓⲉⲡ (probably 'labor, work,' Lyc. reflex of an agricultural-action root) + ⲟⲩⲁⲓⲉ ('farmer'). Recurs in line 16 of the farmer of fields acting as farmer over the soul. The luminaries and the Mind of Light alike perform this farmer-work over the soul-field.

The transcription symbol ⳨ in line 13 is read as ⲣ̄ (the verbal prefix), giving ⲉⲥⲁⲣ̄ ⲛ̄ⲕⲁⲣⲡⲟⲥ 'that she may produce fruits' — standard Coptic ⲣ̄- + Greek loan ⲕⲁⲣⲡⲟⲥ. Same equivalence in line 26 (ⲁⲧⲣⲉⲧⲛⲣ̄ ⲕⲁⲣⲡⲟⲥ). In line 20 (ⲁⲯⲩⲭⲏ) and line 30 (ⲛⲓⲯ[ⲩ]) ⳨ functions as nomen sacrum for ⲯ in ⲯⲩⲭⲏ.

Translated as 'and that they reign and convey her upward,' parsing as conjunctive 3pl ⲛⲥⲉ-ϩⲟⲣⲟ 'and they reign' (cf. ⲛ̄ϩⲟⲣⲟ ⲁⲣⲁ⸗ 'reign over' in glossary) + ⲛⲥⲉ-ⲭⲉⲥⲧⲥ̄ 'and they convey her upward' (cf. ⲭⲉⲥⲧ ⲁⲍⲣⲏⲓ̈ in glossary). The doubled vowels ⲟ̄ⲟ̄ and ⲉⲉ̄ may be Lycopolitan vowel-doubling for the conjunctive prefix.

Translated as 'purity' (tentative). Likely Lyc. reflex of ⲧⲟⲩⲃⲟ 'purity, purification' (cf. ⲡⲧⲟⲩⲃⲟ ⲛ̄ⲭⲭⲡⲟ 'purity of begetting' in glossary), with vowel-shift and the -ⲃⲉ ending preserving the abstract noun-form. Soteriologically: souls ascend through the purity of the Mind of Light. Confidence low; alternative readings include 'channel/conduit' or 'yoke.'
Reading [ⲥⲉ]ⲭ̄ as ⲥⲉⲭⲓ 'they take' (Lyc. ⲭ for ϫ); the idiom ϫⲓ ⲛⲧⲟⲟⲧ⸗ 'take into one's hand' is standard Coptic for 'undertake, receive.' Cf. ⲧⲧ ⲁⲧⲟⲟⲧⲕ̄ 'take into your hand' in glossary.

'Life and Death' — the central Manichaean dualistic pair that the apostles' farmers must manifest to humankind. The exhortation to the elect is to make Life and Death visible to men so that they choose Life and become 'rich.'

Translated as 'there is no power to make you bear fruit' — negative existential ⲙⲛ̄ + ⲟ̄ⲁⲙ 'power' (Lyc. for ϭⲟⲙ; cf. ⲛⲟ̄ⲁⲙ 'powers' in glossary) + causative-infinitive 'to make you bear fruit.' The implication: without proclamation (the act of preaching), the apostles' farming bears no fruit.
Read as Lyc. ⲉⲧⲥⲃⲧⲱⲧ qualitative of ⲥⲟⲃⲧⲉ 'be prepared, made ready.' Translates as 'which is prepared.' The construction ⲉⲧⲥⲃⲧⲱⲧ ⲙ̄ⲙⲉⲩ ⲁⲣⲁⲩ = 'which is prepared there for them.'
Read ⲣⲟⲱⲃ as ⲣ̄-ϩⲱⲃ 'do work, labor' with vowel-doubling and ϩ-loss characteristic of Lycopolitan. The construction is conjunctive 2pl 'and that you should labor in the Spirit.'

ⲛⲟⲩϩⲉ tentatively read as Lyc. variant of ⲛⲟⲩϫⲉ 'cast, throw' in agricultural sense 'sow seed.' 'Land of sowing/casting' fits the harvesting-fruit context of the closing kephalaion. Could alternatively be a plowing-term.
